title: Recurrent gain did not give a consistent bilateral overlap increase beyond direct wiring in two positive worm models
abstract: We tested whether positive recurrent propagation adds a bilateral response overlap effect beyond direct-output overlap and alternative pairings. Two adult C. elegans chemical maps supplied 180 common neurons and 73 bilateral pairs. We used stable linear models, removed the isolated leak response and measured integrated output-trajectory cosine. We compared true pairs with 9,999 right-label permutations within outdegree quartiles. At gain 0.8, count weights increased the bilateral excess over the null mean by 0.0024 and 0.0290 beyond direct output. Upper label ranks were 0.3896 and 0.0001. Binary weights changed the excess by -0.0145 and -0.0080. At gain 0.95, all four map-and-weight combinations lost excess, even as absolute bilateral overlap rose. Thus, absolute convergence and bilateral-specific overlap gave different conclusions. These are conditional model results, not measured activity, information or reliability. Positive effects, equal leaks, partial maps, incomplete pair controls and two adults limit biological use. Original code, aggregate results, a figure, source hashes and separate retrieval steps support reproduction. External record-level materials remain outside the bundle.

display.caption: Response overlap and its bilateral excess in two positive linear worm models. Increasing absolute overlap did not give a consistent increase in the bilateral-specific contrast. No neural activity was measured.
